title: DeleteOutput
description: Records of `delete`: one deleted file, then the terminal summary.

anyOf.title: DeleteOutput
anyOf.description: NDJSON output for a completed delete operation.

bytes.description: File size in bytes before deletion.

checksum_before.description:
BLAKE3 checksum before deletion, absent when the entry has no content.

A regular file and a symlink carry a checksum of what is removed. A
fifo, socket or device is unlinked without being opened, so there is no
content to hash and the field is omitted instead of reporting a hash
that was never computed.

write_strategy.description:
Write strategy this verb used.

`delete` removes the directory entry and never writes file content, so
the value is always `none`; the field exists so a caller that reads a
family of mutating verbs never has to special-case this one.

backup_skipped.description: Why the requested backup was skipped, when the target is itself a copy.

backup_path.description:
Backup file written before the unlink, when one was requested.

The summary counts backups; this fields names the one for this file, so
the caller can restore it without listing the directory.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal warnings about backup flag combinations that had no
effect, e.g. `--keep-backup` on a `delete` that created no copy,
because the verb copies only when the call asks. Empty when there
is nothing to warn about.

anyOf.title: FailureSummary
anyOf.description:
[`Summary`] plus the per-file failure fields; both are omitted when no file failed.

Terminal event of `search`, `replace` and `transform`: a run that reached
every file reads exactly like before, and a run that could not read or write
some files says how many and why instead of staying silent.

files_visited.description:
Total files examined.

`search --target files` counts the files the walk handed over, and
`copy` counts the sources it examined, so a copy that failed is counted
here and in `files_failed` instead of disappearing.

files_matched.description: Files that contributed at least one published answer record.

files_modified.description:
Files actually modified: rewritten by `replace`, `transform`, `case`,
`scope` or `codemod`, deleted by `delete`, copied by `copy`.

files_planned.description:
Files a dry run would have modified.

Present only on a dry run: `files_modified` stays at zero because no
byte changed, and this is the blast radius the caller asked to see. It
is never a claim that the write happened.

files_skipped.description:
Files the run did not answer: binary detection, size cap, no match,
unchanged after a rewrite or an unreadable file. Which of these apply
depends on the verb, and the verb's own section in `HOW_TO_USE` says.

offset_skipped.description: Answer records `search` paged out because `--offset` skipped them.

matches_suppressed.description:
Files where `search --max-count` cut at least one match.

Each file counted here hid at least one more match, so the number is a
floor on what the page left out, not an exact count of the remainder.
The ceiling is on records, not on reading: to prove that a file held
more, the search reads at most one match past the ceiling in that file.

replacements_suppressed.description:
Occurrences `replace --max-replacements` left unchanged.

The verb counts every occurrence of `old` before it applies the ceiling,
so this is exact and the agent can size the second run from it.

below_min_score.description:
Lines `semantic-search --min-score` discarded for scoring below it.

A zero-match answer with a high floor is otherwise indistinguishable from
a tree that has nothing to say about the query.

files_read.description:
Files opened and read, the stage between the walk handing a path over
and the scoring that decides whether it answers.

files_budget_dropped.description:
Items the `--limit` budget cut before the verb worked on them.

The unit is the one the verb produces: files for a verb that walks
paths, records for a verb that streams them.

backups_kept.description:
Backups this run created and left on disk.

A destructive verb that keeps a copy must say so: the caller decides
whether the bytes are still there, and silence read as "removed".

backup_bytes.description: Bytes those backups occupy on disk.

dirs_left.description: Directories the run could not remove because entries remained.

hint.description:
One sentence telling the caller what to change to finish the job.

`dirs_left` counts the leftovers, and the count alone leaves the reader
to guess why. The hint appears only when the run itself asked to skip
entries, through `--include`, `--exclude`, `--older-than` or `--limit`,
so it names the filter that kept the directory in place.

files_total.description:
Files the progress precount found eligible, published only when that
precount ran (`--progress-every` on and quiet off); it is the total the
run is working through, not the page it published.

binary_rejects.description:
Files refused because they hold binary content, a subset of
`files_skipped` that lets the agent tell a binary refusal from a size cap
or an unchanged rewrite.

total_matches.description:
Answer records actually published, after `--limit` and `--offset`; for
`transform` and `transform --rules` it is the replacements performed,
and for `scope` it is the scopes matched across every file.

total_replacements.description: Total replacements performed across all files.

total_bytes.description:
Bytes the run left on disk or moved: the size after a rewrite, the size
copied, or the size hashed, depending on the verb.

walker_stopped_early.description: Present and true when the walker itself quit before the tree ended.

files_failed.description:
Files that matched or were visited but could not be processed, plus
the root named in the invocation that does not exist.

partial.description:
The run answered from part of its targets, so the answer is partial.

Present exactly when `files_failed` is present, so a consumer reads one
flag instead of comparing two counters. A run that reached every file
keeps the shape it always had.

errors.description:
First failures, capped at `summary.errors_max_entries` (50 by default);
`files_failed` is the full count.

ok.description: Outcome of the run, stamped by the writer

code.description: Machine error code, present when ok is false

exit.description: Process exit status, present when ok is false

target_resolved.description: Absolute targets the run resolved, in invocation order, and never a joined string, so a path holding `,` stays readable; a run with one target publishes a one-item array, so the shape never depends on the count

target_source.description: Where the target came from: named in the invocation line, inherited from the workspace slot, or the standard-input stream

workspace_source.description: Where the workspace root came from: the `--workspace` flag or the process working directory

records_suppressed.description: Records the writer dropped before the terminal event: `--filter` rejections, `--select` projections that emptied the record, dedupe duplicates and `--limit` cuts. It counts records, never files, so it does not compare with `files_matched`: one file can contribute several records

truncated.description: The record itself was cut by `--truncate-content` or `--max-output-bytes`, so the fields are shorter than the source

truncated_records.description: Records the writer cut this run, counted once per record

line_end.description: 1-based last line of that block, when the block spans more than a line.

line.description:
1-based line of the block that holds the syntax error (v0.1.38).

Present only for [`AtomwriteError::SyntaxError`]. Without it the caller
had to re-read the file to learn where the refusal points.

pairs_applied.description:
Pairs that were written to the target before the error (v0.1.37).

Always `0` for the all-or-nothing `EditPairFailed` abort (nothing is
written) and `total - unmatched` for `edit-loop --partial`.

path.description: Filesystem path related to the error, if applicable.

error_class.description: Error class: transient, conflict, `precondition_failed`, or permanent.

retryable.description: Whether a retry may resolve this error.

suggestion.description: Optional actionable suggestion for the caller.

suggestion_lang.description:
Language of `suggestion` when it is not English, so a consumer knows
what it is reading.

workspace.description: Workspace root used for jail validation, if applicable.

failed_pair_index.description: 1-based index of the failed `--old`/`--new` pair (multi-pair edit, G117).

pairs_total.description:
Total number of `--old`/`--new` pairs in the invocation.

Emitted by multi-pair edit (G117) and by a partial `edit-loop` run
(v0.1.36) — one key, two producers.

pair_results.description:
Per-pair diagnostics up to and including the failed pair (multi-pair edit, G117).
Pairs after the failure were never attempted and are absent.

best_candidate.description: Closest near-miss when a match cascade fails (v0.1.29 P0-2).

match_count.description: Match count when ambiguity is reported (v0.1.30).

similar_paths.description: Similar basenames when path is missing (v0.1.30).

conflict_count.description: Number of conflicting regions a three-way merge could not align (v0.1.36).

missing_flag.description:
Flag literal the operation required but did not receive (v0.1.36).

Present only for [`AtomwriteError::MissingFlag`]; the duplicate `code`
on that variant is deliberate — callers branch on `missing_flag` and
still see the `INVALID_INPUT` family in `code`.

pairs_unmatched.description:
Pairs that did not match in a partial `edit-loop` run (v0.1.36).

`pairs_total` already exists above for the multi-pair edit family and
is reused by this variant instead of being duplicated.

anyOf.title: ErrorJson
anyOf.description: Serializable error envelope emitted as a single NDJSON line.

ok.description:
Always false on error envelopes (GAP-2026-020 agent sentinel).

`ok: false` together with `code` is the whole verdict: the redundant
`error: true` duplicate left the envelope because every failure paid
for it and no caller branched on it alone.

exit.description: Process exit status this failure maps to.

path.description: Filesystem path related to the error, if applicable.

error_class.description: Error class: transient, conflict, `precondition_failed`, or permanent.

retryable.description: Whether a retry may resolve this error.

suggestion.description: Optional actionable suggestion for the caller.

Present only for [`AtomwriteError::SyntaxError`]. Without it the caller

target_resolved.description: Absolute targets the run resolved, in invocation order, and never a joined string, so a path holding `,` stays readable; a run with one target publishes a one-item array, so the shape never depends on the count

target_source.description: Where the target came from: named in the invocation line, inherited from the workspace slot, or the standard-input stream

records_suppressed.description: Records the writer dropped before the terminal event: `--filter` rejections, `--select` projections that emptied the record, dedupe duplicates and `--limit` cuts. It counts records, never files, so it does not compare with `files_matched`: one file can contribute several records

files_budget_dropped.description: Entries the `--limit` budget dropped, in the unit the verb produces: files for walking verbs, records for streaming ones; a floor, because workers may stop before producing the rest

files_planned.description: Files the run would have modified in `--dry-run` or `--preview`; absent from a run that really wrote

truncated.description: The record itself was cut by `--truncate-content` or `--max-output-bytes`, so the fields are shorter than the source

truncated_records.description: Records the writer cut this run, counted once per record

FileFailure.description: One file an operation could not process, as listed in a summary's `errors[]`.

path.description: Path of the file that failed.

code.description: Machine error code of the failure (for example `PERMISSION_DENIED`).

PairResult.description:
Outcome of matching a single `--old`/`--new` pair in multi-pair edit mode.

Emitted in `pair_results` on both success and error envelopes so agents
can verify each pair objectively without re-running the edit (G117).
In the default all-or-nothing mode, pairs after the first failure are
never attempted and are absent from the array.

index.description: 1-based position of the pair in the `--old`/`--new` invocation order.

matched.description: Whether the pair matched and was applied to the content.

similarity.description: Similarity score of the fuzzy match, 0.0-1.0 (block-anchor and context-aware only).

source.description: Source of the match/replacement content: `"arg"` or `"file"`.

BestCandidate.description:
Closest near-miss when a fuzzy/exact match fails (v0.1.29 P0-2).

Agents use this to correct `old` without re-reading the full file.

text.description: Snippet of the best matching region (truncated to 500 chars).

line.description: 1-based line of the candidate start in the file.

similarity.description: Similarity score 0.0–1.0 of the best attempt.

strategy.description: Strategy that produced this candidate score.
